div.head: Further: the Book of Daniel. Twelve sections.

div.ab: First, the proem. Daniel the prophet was the son of Jeconiah, the son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah. ⁵And he was a man who kept himself from women, and because he was beardless it is supposed that he was an eunuch. And in the first year that Nebuchadnezzar reigned in Babylon, i.e., in the third year of Jehoiakim, he went up against Jerusalem and took away the vessels for the (temple) service; and Daniel himself, and Hananiah and Azariah and Mishael, his uncles, sons of Jehoiakim, he took as hostages and ¹⁰carried them down with him to Babylon. And he prophesied there during the entire period of the captivity. And he died in Babylon and was buried in Shushan the castle, which is in the city of Elam.

div.head: Section First.
div.ab:
(1:1) Nebuchadnezzar, i.e., image of Nebo, which is Zeus. (1:2) To the land of Shinar, i.e., Babylon. (1:3) Ashpåz, prince of the eunuchs. Greek: chief of the eunuchs. (1:5) Parthians, i.e., Kurds, Assyrians. The daily portion,
<with å of j and fricativeness of t; Nestorians: with stopping of t>. Greek: Allowance ¹⁵<with s>, i.e., daily ration. (1:7) And the prince of the eunuchs gave them names. He called Daniel Belteshazzar, i.e., image of Bel, which is Zeus. Shadrach, i.e., messenger. Meshach <with a of m, and in old codices i of m>, i.e., the anointer of the earth. Abed-nego, i.e., universal servant. (1:8) And Daniel determined in his mind that he would not eat of the delicacies of the king, i.e., of the things cooked. Greek: that he would not defile himself with the supper of the king. (1:10) Who has given commandment concerning ²⁰your eating and concerning your drinking <with i of t> that he might not see your faces unsightly, i.e., altered by disease. (1:11) And Daniel said to Manisar. Greek: to Abiezer. (1:16) He took away their provisions, i.e., their allowance. (2:4) And the Chaldeans spoke before the king in Aramaic. Greek: Syriac,<i.e., with a of ʾ and r and m from Aram-naharain. The Nestorians read incorrectly with a of ʾ and vowellessness of r, because Armaeans, with a of ʾ, means heathens>. (2:7) And its interpretation - Greek: ²⁵its explanation - we will show. (2:9) If you do not show me
the dream your judgment is one <with å of d>, i.e., your purpose, for you have conspired to deceive. (2:15) Why is the decree urgent? <with a of m and ṣ>, i.e., harsh. Greek: bitter.

div.head: Section Second.
div.ab:
(2:28) Thy dream and the vision of thy head, i.e., the dream (comes about) by means of the imaginative power which is (located) in the front part of the brain. (2:31) And behold, an image, a great one, i.e., a type of the world. (2:32) Its head (was) of gold, i.e., the kingdom of the Babylonians. Its breast and its arms ³⁰of silver, i.e., the kingdom of the Medes. Its belly and thighs of copper, i.e., the kingdom of the Persians. (2:33) Its legs of iron, i.e., the kingdom of Alexander. Its feet part of iron and part of earthenware, i.e., the kingdom of the servants who ruled after him. (2:34) And thou sawest that the rock was cut out without hands, i.e., the spiritual kingdom of our Lord the Messiah, which would break in pieces and bring to an end all the kingdoms of the ³⁵world, but it would stand forever. (2:40) Smiting <with r> - i.e., crushing - and breaking in pieces, <in some codices, grinding to powder>. (3:1) In the plain
of Dura, i.e., mesa. (3:3) The ʾArgådhåjē and the Garbᵉdhåjē and the Tarbᵉdhåjē and the Tīvtåjē.
The zither, with one hand they hold the strings and with the other they play (cf. 3:5). And the lyre they play with both hands. And the bagpipe, i.e., the flute.

div.head: Section Third.
div.ab: (3:16) We have no need to answer thee a word concerning this matter, i.e., there was not a thing that he needed to hear or consider. (3:19) And he ordered to heat the furnace seven times, i.e., more than at any (other) time. (3:21) They bound ⁵them in their trousers and in their leggings, i.e., in the puttees which covered their legs. (3:22) And those men who had slandered them, the flame killed them, i.e., when they approached to see how they were burning they (themselves) were burnt, and this (occurred) that the Babylonians and the king might not suppose that that fire was imaginary and not real. But Daniel he did not cast with these three into the furnace of fire because ¹⁰he was called by the name of the idol Bel, or because he was afraid of him after he had interpreted his dream. (3:38) And there is not at this time a ruler or a prince, neither a prophet nor a governor, i.e., who would be able to help.

div.head: Section Fourth.
div.ab:
(3:49) But the angel of
dew came down and quenched the flame, i.e., a sign that over all created things angels have power to govern. (3:86) Bless the Lord, all breaths - Greek: spirits and souls - of the righteous; glorify and exalt him, <with å of ḥ>. (3:74) O earth, ¹⁵bless - Greek: Let bless - the Lord. Glorify and exalt him, <with i of ḥ and m>. Greek: Let her glorify and greatly exalt him, <with e of ḥ and m>. (3:76) Bless the Lord, all herbs of the earth. Greek: all things that grow upon the earth. (3:92) And the aspect of the fourth is like a son of the gods, i.e., the angel who quenched the flame. (3:94) And the smell of fire had not passed over them, i.e., did not cling (to them). (4:10) A tree in the midst of the earth whose ²⁰height was great, i.e., a type of Nebuchadnezzar himself. (4:12) Its leaves were beautiful, i.e., a type of his armies. And its fruit abundant, i.e., a type of his princes. The beasts of the field, and in its branches dwelt all the fowls of heaven, i.e., a type of the peoples and kingdoms that were under his dominion. And from it all flesh was fed, i.e., with his stamp were stamped the zuze and dinars everywhere. (4:15) But leave the stump of its roots in the earth, i.e., a type of ²⁵his kingship
which continued until he returned. With a band of iron and copper in the tender grass of the field, i.e., a type of his continuing in the wilderness and of his nourishment which was from the grass. (4:16) And his heart shall be changed from humankind, i.e., his mental disease would be a form of insanity. And the heart of an animal shall be given to him, i.e., with the animals he would mingle and he would not be afraid of them. And seven periods shall pass over him, i.e., three years and a half, each ³⁰period six months. (4:17) By the command of the watcher is the word, i.e., an angel spoke these things. And in the saying of the holy one is the matter, i.e., for what he had said interpretation is required. And the basest of men ho setteth up over it <with e of p. Nestorians: with a of p>, i.e., his wife and his son Evil-Merodach, whom he imprisoned after he returned.

div.head: Section Fifth.
div.ab:
(4:23) And destroy it <with vowellessness of b>, in the imperative. (4:24) The decree of the Most High is at hand, i.e., ³⁵of God. (4:26) (Is) enduring, <with a of q and å of i>. (4:27) Therefore let my counsel be acceptable to thee, and thy sins redeem by almsgiving and thine iniquities by mercy toward the lowly, i.e., following the example of Joseph who, when he had interpreted the dream to Pharaoh, counselled these things as advantageous. (4:29) And after twelve months, i.e.,
patience was (extended) to him that he might repent, even though his heart became
more hardened. (4:31) A voice came from heaven, To thee it is said, O King Nebuchadnezzar, i.e., a type of the Trinity. (4:34) And my understanding returned to me <with a of m and d>, i.e., it came back. (5:1) Belteshazzar the king made a great feast for his thousand princes, i.e., after Nebuchadnezzar died Evil-merodach his eldest son reigned ⁵two years and died, and Belteshazzar his younger brother reigned in his stead. But some say that Belteshazzar was the son of Evil-merodach, that this might be fulfilled, The peoples shall serve him and his son and his son's son, (cf. Jer. 27:7), that is to say, Nebuchadnezzar's. And he was drinking wine before the thousand, i.e., in the great company and not in secret, as was the custom with kings. (5:2) And Belteshazzar commanded, while under the influence of his wine <with e of t>, i.e., in ¹⁰his drunkenness. (5:6) His countenance was changed and the joints of his loins were loosed, <with vowellessness of t>. (5:10) And the queen, i.e., the mother of Belteshazzar.

div.head: Section Sixth.
div.ab:
(5:25) Mᵉnē, mᵉnå Nestorians: Mᵉnē, mᵉnē, with e of both ns>, i.e., God has indeed numbered the years of thy kingdom and cut them short.
Tᵉkal wᵉpharsīn, i.e., having weighed thee and found thee wanting in all righteousness he stretched out the hand of the Persians over thy kingdom. And the Greek says, Maʾni, Pares, Teqel. ¹⁵And Pares may be explained as a breach because also Pereṣ the son of Judah was named Breach from this (circumstance) that the midwife said exultingly, Thou hast made a breach for thyself (cf. Gen. 38:29). (5:29) And Daniel was clothed with purple, i.e., making his heart glad, perhaps to persuade his God to remove his anger from him. (5:30) In that very night Belteshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain, i.e., when, because of anxiety about the vision, he went out of his bed-chamber by night as far as the guard. They thought ²⁰that he was a foreigner who had come among them to kill the king, and they smote him and killed him. (5:31) And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, i.e., although he was of the seed of the Medes, yet he reigned over the kingdom of the Chaldeans and was numbered with them. (6:10) And three times a day he knelt down upon his knees and prayed, i.e., because he was busy about royal matters he was able to pray only three times.

div.head: Section Seventh.
div.ab:
²⁵(6:17) And the king sealed it with his signet, i.e., because he was afraid lest his enemies might do away with him. And with the signet of his princes, i.e., lest they should come and say that food was given to the lions and therefore they did not eat Daniel. (6:18) And he passed the night without
food - Greek: And he passed the night fasting - i.e., because of his distress over Daniel. (6:22) And they closed, <with vowellessness of s>. (6:24) Them and their wives and their children, i.e., because all of them were bent on the destruction ³⁰of Daniel. (7:2) And behold, the four winds of the heavens making the great sea rage, i.e., the world (by) the angels who are set in control over its four quarters. (7:3) And four beasts, i.e., the kingdoms of the Babylonians and Medes and Persians and Greeks. (7:4) And it was lifted up from the earth, i.e., a type of its dissolution. And the heart of a man was given to it, i.e., fearful. (7:5) And it rose up on one side, i.e., ruling over a portion of the earth. And three ribs in its mouth, ³⁵i.e., Babylon and Media and Persia. Arise, devour much flesh, i.e., booty. (7:6) Four wings and four heads, i.e., ruling over the four quarters. (7:7) And it was different, i.e., the Babylonians and Medes and Persians were related to one another in speech and location,
but the Greeks differed from them. It had ten horns, i.e., ten kings who should descend from Alexander. (7:8) And I considered its horns, i.e., gave attention to. And one little horn, i.e., Antiochus, the persecutor. And three of the first horns were uprooted,
i.e., he ⁵subdued Asia and Egypt and Persia. And eyes like the eyes of a man, i.e., crafty. (7:9) I was seeing thrones being set up, i.e., a type of the honor prepared for the prophets and apostles; if it were otherwise the spiritual throne upon which the God of all is exalted is one. And the Ancient of Days was sitting, i.e., the Eternal one. (7:10) A stream of fire was issuing, and going forth from before him, i.e., a type of the greatness of his vengeance. A thousand thousands ministered ¹⁰unto him and ten thousand ten thousands stood before him, i.e., the greatness of the number of the angelic hosts is meant and not a definite number. The judge sat and the books were opened <with a of p>, i.e., expressed according to human custom, because a book is not necessary for the one who is inerrant. (7:13) I was seeing upon the clouds of heaven one like a human being came, i.e., literally Zerubbabel, but spiritually our Lord. (7:16) And the significance of my words he made me to understand, ¹⁵i.e., the interpretation. (7:18) The holy ones of the Most High, i.e., the Maccabees.

div.head: Section Eighth.
div.ab:
(7:19) The fourth beast, i.e., to this one a name was not given as to the others, since it was composite of many peoples. And teeth of iron and claws of copper, i.e., a type of the strength of the armies of the Greeks. (7:23) And it shall break it in pieces, <with a of t>. (7:25) And they shall be given into
his hand unto a time, times, and half a time. Greek: unto a time and times and unto half a time, i.e., three years and six months, the duration of the persecution of Antiochus, for a time is one year and times is two years and half a time is ²⁰half a year. Because at the expiration of this time Antiochus the persecutor died, in the region of the Persians, and the Maccabees began to be victorious. (8:2) A portico, i.e., a gateway, like a vestibule (?). Ulai, i.e., the name of a river. (8:3) And behold a ram, i.e., Darius II, who lunged at men wickedly. And he had horns, i.e., the Medes and Persians. And the one that was higher sprang up last, i.e., this refers to the fact that it was the Persians who ruled after the Medes and were superior to them. (8:5) ²⁵And a kid of the goats, i.e., Alexander was called a kid because he did not greatly harm men. And a horn between his eyes, i.e., his kingdom was strengthened by wisdom. (8:8) And his great horn was borken, i.e., a type of his death. And from under it came up four conspicuous ones - Greek: after it - , i.e., four of his servants who reigned after him. (8:9) And from one of them there went forth one little horn, Antiochus, who ³⁰was weaker than the rest. And the hosts and the stars (cf. 8:10) he called the Maccabees and Onias and Eliezar because they feared God. (8:11) And from him he took away the continual(sacrifice), i.e., he caused the sacrifices to cease. (8:12)And a host
was set against the continual (sacrifice) because of sins, i.e., by reason of the sins of the people he became strengthened against them. (8:13) And one holy one said to a certain other <with vowellessness of m and i of n>, i.e., a certain one who was an initiate and was revealing the mysteries to me. (8:14) Unto two ³⁵thousand and three hundred day-and-nights <with e of m and a of p>, i.e., by the expression day-and-nights the prophet indicates the severity of the persecution; that is to say, he counts each day of the persecution as two. And this is clear from the fact that half this number, that is to say, a thousand and a hundred and fifty
days make approximately three lunar years and three months, because a lunar year is about three hundred and fifty days. And at the end of this period Antiochus departed for Persia and the persecution ceased, and three months later, that is to say, at the end of three years and a half, he died there, ⁵and the people were delivered from his wickedness. And righteousness shall prevail - Greek: The holy place shall be cleansed - , i.e., after the persecutor dies Judah the righteous Maccabee shall prevail and he shall cleanse the temple, which the pagans defiled with their idols. (8:16) Gabriel, i.e., when the advent of our Lord drew nigh
the harbinger of his birth appeared. (8:24) And not by his own strength, i.e., God was setting him in authority that he might chastise the people with his rod. And he shall pervert the miracles, i.e., ¹⁰he shall annul the divine law. (8:25) And he shall pervert many secretly, i.e., by treachery. And the potentate of potentates, i.e., God. And in the turning of a hand he shall be broken, i.e., suddenly. (8:26b) Conceal this vision, i.e., lest when the Gentiles hear they be hindered from going up against Jerusalem. And the vision of the day-and-nights that was told is the truth, i.e., the number of days that is specified.

div.head: Section Ninth.
div.ab:
(9:2) I Daniel ¹⁵perceived by the book the number of years, i.e., I saw.....that there were completed for the desolation of Jerusalem the seventy years, at whose expiration Jeremiah the prophet said the people would return from Babylon. (9:3) I lifted up my face before the Lord God to make entreaty by prayer and supplication, i.e., lest by reason of the sins of the people they stay more than seventy in Babylon, just like the thirty more than the four hundred ²⁰which God had said to Abraham his seed lingered in Egypt. (9:21)And [the man] Gabriel whom I had seen in the former vision flew swiftly. Greek: having come swiftly. (9:23)At the beginning of thy prayer the word went forth. Greek: the command. And
I have come to show thee because thou art well-pleasing. Greek: because thou hast obtained mercy. (9:24) Seventy weeks, - i.e., four hundred and ninety years - shall rest - i.e., pass - upon thy people ²⁵and upon the city of thy holiness to pay fully the debts and to complete the sins, for forgiveness of iniquity and for the attainment of the righteousness which is unto everlasting - Greek: everlasting righteousness - , i.e., in this period the people cultivate righteousness, when returning and building Jerusalem. (9:25) And to the coming of Messiah, the King, i.e., and at that time they would become guilty of slaying him and the sword would prevail over them. And as to these weeks, ³⁰they should be counted from the beginning of the twentieth year of Artaxerxes Longimanus, when he sent Ezra the scribe and Nehemiah the cupbearer and they built the temple and the city, unto the end of the fourth year of Gaius who erected in the temple that idol concerning which our Lord said, When you see the sign of abomination of desolation spoken of in Daniel (Cf. Mt. 24:15), and not from the beginning of the reign ³⁵of Cyrus, when he caused fifty thousand to go up from captivity and commanded them to build the temple. Otherwise, the sum total is one hundred and thirteen years more than the seventy weeks, as
is shown in the chronological table. Seven weeks and
sixty-two weeks, i.e., after he had mentioned the number seventy weeks as a sum total, then again he divided it into three portions. The first portion is seven weeks, the second portion sixty-two weeks, the third portion one week and half a week. And because this division exceeds the seventy weeks by half a week, ⁵commentators say the seven weeks are the years of the building of the temple, which was built in forty-sixyears, as the Jews told our Lord, that is to say, three years fewer than the seven weeks, but this deficiency is supplied by the excess of half a week. And as for this, what would it have come to if the seventy weeks had been counted from the first building in the time of Cyrus? Now, as for this, it is indeed not so, as we have said, ¹⁰and the sixty-two weeks are the four hundred and thirty-four years from the completion of the building of the temple, according to the view of commentators, to the crucifixion of our Lord, as the prophet himself says that after the sixty-two weeks (9:26) the Messiah shall be killed. Greek:the anointing shall be far off. Hebrew: the ointment shall
cease and no man shall be anointed as priest, i.e., no king would arise again for the Jews. And the town of the saints shall be corrupted with the ¹⁵king that comes, i.e., with Gaius, who profaned the temple. And there shall not be for her, that is, for Jerusalem another anointed one. (9:27) And he shall strengthen the covenant for many, i.e., the Messiah himself for the Gentiles who believe in him. One week and half of a week, i.e., this is the third portion, that is to say, the time from the Passion until the temple was defiled. And it is evident that this time is a year and a half short of the time of which the prophet spoke, because there are ²⁰nine years all told from the beginning of the nineteenth year of Tiberius, in which our Lord suffered, unto the end of the fourth year of Gaius, in which he introduced the idol into the temple. And he shall cause to cease sacrifice and offering, i.e., the bloody sacrifices from the Jews. And upon the wings of the abomination desolation unto the end of the judgments, i.e., desolation shall rule over the Jews forever. (10:2) I Daniel sat in mourning, i.e., when ²⁵I perceived the evils that were ready to befall the children of my people.

div.head: Section Tenth.
div.ab:
(10:6) And his appearance was distinctive and quite unique, i.e., Gabriel the angel, whose aspect was different from the likeness of men. (10:11) And he said to me, Arise, Daniel, thou man of esteem - Greek: And he said to me, Daniel, thou art a man who obtains mercy
- i.e., the angel encouraged him, because there was no strength left in him on account of fear, and in that year ³⁰he died. (10:13) And the guardian angel of the king of Persia stood up against me twenty-one days, i.e., in these three weeks of his mourning; and this angel was not willing that the request of the prophet should be granted because of the good that would come to his people from intercourse with the people of the law. And behold, Michael, one of the first princes, came to help me, i.e., because he was the guiding (angel) of the first ³⁵and ancient covenant just as Gabriel is of the new, and hence evidence that every people has a guiding angel. (10:21) But I will show thee the thing that is written in the book of verity - Greek: In the writing of truth - , i.e., which Moses wrote in Deuteronomy. I know
that after my death you will become utterly corrupt and evil will befall you in the latter days. (Cf. Dt. 31:29). And there was no one who was helping me.....except Michael, your guardian and I, i.e., Gabriel says, I and Michael alone were importuning God for the deliverance of the Hebrews, and the rest of the angels, ⁵when they saw their evil bent, did not wish that they be set free. (11:2) Yet three kings shall arise in Persia,i.e., Artaxerxes the Mindful and
Artaxerxes Ochus and Persis. And the fourth shall grow rich, i.e., Darius son of Arsaces, who was the tenth from Cyrus and whom Alexander killed. (11:3) And a mighty king shall arise, i.e., Alexander. (11:4) And it shall be scattered to the four winds of the heavens, i.e., his four ¹⁰servants who were brought up with him, Seleucus who reigned in Babylon and built Seleucia and Ctesiphon, and Ptolemy in Egypt, and Antiochus in Syria, and another Seleucus in Antioch. And not according to his sword and not according to his power, i.e., the duration of the kingdom of Alexander was [not] in accordance with its greatness. And there is no other beside these, i.e., no man is to rule except his servants. (11:5) And ¹⁵the king of the south shall become strong, i.e., the Ptolemy who drove out Alexander the younger, son of Antiochus Epiphanes. (11:6) And at the end of years they shall come to agreement, i.e., become reconciled. And the daughter of the king of the south shall go unto the king of the north, that is, Cleopatra, the daughter of Ptolemy will be given as wife to Alexander the younger. And there shall not be in her strength because of fear, i.e., lest her husband bring
the wickedness of her father upon her head. ²⁰And she shall be given up and they that brought her....and they that strengthened her, i.e., her father took her from him by guile and gave her to his enemy Demetrius. (11:7) And from the rootstock of his seed one shall arise upon his place, i.e., Antiochus, who was of the seed of Alexander. (11:11) And the king of the south shall be provoked, i.e., Ptolemy. And he shall go out to encounter the king of the north, i.e., Alexander. (11:15) And the arm of the ²⁵south shall not stand, i.e., Demetrius, to whom Ptolemy gave his daughter so that he might help him. (11:17) And a daughter of men shall be given him to destroy him, i.e., in guile Ptolemy gave his daughter to Alexander that she might put him to death. And when she found it impossible, he took her from him and gave her to Demetrius; and this is that (which he says) she shall not rise up and shall not be his.

div.head: Section Eleventh.
div.ab:
(11:18) And a prince who has reviled him he shall remove, i.e., Alexander, ³⁰whom he had set over Cilicia. (11:21) And there shall rise up in his place a feeble one, that is, Demetrius instead of Alexander. And the glory of the kingdoms shall not be given unto him, i.e., his princes hated him and shut her up in Antioch. And he shall come secretly, i.e., Antiochus,
son of Demetrius. (11:24) And he shall go up and become strong with a small people, i.e. that of the Hebrews. (11:26) And those eating his dainties shall break him, i.e., ³⁵Tryphon, who betrayed and killed Antiochus. (11:27) And both of the kings, i.e., Antiochus and Tryphon. (11:30) And he shall show regard to those who have abandoned the holy covenant, i.e., Antiochus would make friends with the priests who were repudiating the law. (11:31) And they shall deliver the abomination to destruction, i.e., the Maccabees, who in divine strength destroyed the abomination.
(11:32) And those who do wickedly against the covenant he shall win over, i.e., those of the people transgressing the law. (11:33) And by spoliation a thousand days, i.e., with violent persecution they would be afflicted. (11:35) And some of the wise shall be overthrown to make trial among them, i.e., from the priests and scribes who were perishing the ⁵common people learned that they were persecuted because they had forsaken the law. And for discernment unto the time of the end, i.e., in the end the facts would be
known. (11:36) And the king shall do according to his desire, i.e., Antiochus would oppress the people and blaspheme God. (11:45) And he shall set up <with e of n> his tent in a level place, i.e., between the Red Sea and Mount Horeb. And he shall preserve his sanctuary, i.e., his people. (12:1) From the days of old, <with å of m>. Of the children of thy people every one shall be delivered who is found ¹⁰written in the book, i.e., a few whom the mercy of God shall preserve. (12:2) And the many who sleep <with a of d> in the dust shall awake - i.e., the Maccabees - some to everlasting life - i.e., those who endure temptations - and some to perdition, i.e., those who apostatized. (12:3) And they that make many victorious, i.e., the Maccabees. (12:4) And thou Daniel, seal up these words and keep silent, i.e., that the people might not hear and be afraid, ¹⁵and not return to Jerusalem. For in the first year that Cyrus the Persian reigned he gave the people (permission) to return and there went up of the captivity of the Jews fifty thousand. And he commanded that they build a house for the Lord. But it was delayed by the people who were round about them until the
sixth year of Darius the son of Hystaspis, which was forty-six years, as it is written in the Gospel of John. (12:7) And he swore ²⁰by him that liveth forever, i.e., the angel that Daniel saw, who was clad in magnificent raiment. For unto a time, times, and half a time, i.e., during the three years and a half when the Greeks ruled over the people and defiled the temple. And in the time when the hands of all the holy people shall be delivered - i.e., of the Maccabees - all these things shall be completed, i.e., Antiochus would die and persecution would cease, and ²⁵the temple would be cleansed of idols. (12:11) The abomination shall be given up to destruction a thousand and two hundred and ninety days. (12:12) Blessed is he who shall tarry that he may attain to the thousand and three hundred and thirty-five days, i.e., the first number he mentioned lacked forty-five of the other number. And it seems that he says that from the beginning of the persecution of Antiochus unto the completion, for a thousand days the pollution would be at its height, and after ³⁰this two hundred and ninety days would intervene, and forty-five days after this defilement would completely cease. But according to some, the first number typifies the rule of Antichrist, and the second the coming of Elijah, and the third the advent of our Lord from heaven.

div.head: Section Twelfth.
div.ab:
The story of the idol Bel. ³⁵Some do not accept this story, nor that of the dragon, and they say that Daniel was cast into the den of lions one time, and not twice. (verse 1) And King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, i.e., Cyrus the Persian killed Astyages the king of the Medes and Darius the king
of the Babylonians, and he established the kingdom of the Persians. (verse 3) Now the Babylonians had an idol and its name was Bel, i.e., Zeus. And the astrologers say Bel was the star of [Ba]bylon, and from it they determined concerning it (Babylon) good and evil. Twelve artaba of fine flour - i.e., an artaba was a measure that contained twelve makuke - ⁵and six metretai of wine, i.e., a metrete is a measure which contains six Edessene measures. Now the priests were eating and drinking these and saying that the idol was nourished by them. (verse 21) And they showed the king the entrance - Greek:the feet of the doors - which they had in secret. (verse 22) And Bel - Greek: the provision of Bel - he gave to Daniel, i.e., the gold wherewith it had been overlaid. Further, the dragon. (verse 27) And ¹⁰Daniel took pitch - Greek: thirty minas of pitch - and hair and fat.......
.....and the dragon swallowed them, i.e., the balls. And it burst open with vowellessness of b and died. (verse 32) And there were given to them - i.e., to the seven lions that were in the den - two bodies - i.e., of those who were condemned to death - and two rams, i.e., of the flock. (verse 33) Now there was a prophet Habakkuk in Judea and he had made pottage, and there were broken pieces of bread in a bowl and he put (them) ¹⁵in it. In Greek there is an addition: and a xestes of mixed wine. (verse 36) And he lifted him up by the hair of his head and set him in Babylon above the den, by the power of the Holy Spirit. In the Greek this last phraseis omitted.
